newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end a shade weaker, Dow supports.
newsitem.headline: German shares end a shade weaker, Dow supports.

text.p: German blue-chip shares pared some of the losses from bourse dealings in late IBIS electronic dealings, underpinned by strength on Wall Street.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day computer dealings, recovered from the day's lows to end down just 2.61 points, or 0.10 percent, at 2,702.60 points.
The 30-share DAX index of blue-chip stocks had closed the bourse session down 11.47 points at 2,691.17.
After so many consecutive record highs, dealers said a period of consolidation was a healthy sign and said the day's weakness was not the beginning of a reversal.
Dealers said they would look to Wall Street for direction, although the Dow Jones index was also seen to be in a consolidation phase just below the 6,000 level.
"The Americans must decide in which direction we are heading," said one trader. " But until the U.S. election we expect the market to continue to be positive."
Dealers said the German market was awaiting the release of U.S. retail sales and producer price data scheduled for Friday.
They said the unexpectedly strong rise in German seasonally-adjusted unemployment had little impact on shares.

Metals group Metallgesellschaft AG was the day's best performer on the DAX, gaining over four percent after saying profits for the 1995/1996 financial year would top the previous year. MG ended post-bourse trade up 1.80 at 29.05.
MG officials said the firm had done "extraordinarily well" under difficult conditions.
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas jumped 6.10 marks or over two percent in pre-bourse trade to a new high at 148 marks after announcing it would be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer World Cup.
Adidas ended IBIS dealings 3.10 marks higher at 145 marks.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa also moved against the trend, hitting a pre-bourse session high of 224.90 marks after it said a co-operative alliance with Scandinavian airline SAS would improve its net earnings by 100 million marks in 1997.
Later Lufthansa shares came off somewhat and ended IBIS trade at 224.00 marks, up two marks.
